decisions.decision: The measured defect, re-read by the coordinator at 76cfa91 rather than taken from V2-082's evidence. Service.Plan (internal/application/service.go:882-966) and Service.Prepare (service.go:986-1041) contain ZERO references to domain.Permit, domain.Controls, domain.EffectiveControl or domain.EffectFromPermit: `awk 'NR>=882 && NR<=1042' internal/application/service.go | grep -n 'Permit\|Controls\|EffectiveControl'` returns nothing. Both change canonical state anyway. Plan writes the parent Requirement (u.SaveRequirement at service.go:939, appending an Increment id and incrementing Version), creates an Increment at IncrementProposed (u.SaveIncrement, service.go:942), writes a canonical target and records an increment.proposed event. Prepare drives domain.DecideIncrement with Kind IncrementPrepare and saves the Increment at IncrementReady. The full non-test census of domain.Permit call sites is eleven -- framing.go:183, repository.go:128, outbox.go:448, human_input.go:644, service.go:415, :664, :824, :1228, :1469, :1669 and the EffectFromPermit at :1673 -- and Plan and Prepare are in none of them. So under emergency-stop, the one mode docs/product/definition.md section 7 describes as stopping every repository, every worker and every version, a caller can still create an Increment, move a Requirement's version and make an Increment claimable. A stop that still permits canonical state to move is not a stop.
decisions.rationale: Every figure above is to be RE-MEASURED by the implementer; the last eleven tasks each found at least one stale number in a Work Order. The defect was first observed by V2-082, which recorded it as a finding and deliberately did not repair it because internal/application/service.go was prohibited to that task: internal/application/framing_test.go:565 TestPlanAndPrepareAreMeasuredUnderEmergencyStop drives Plan and Prepare under an effective emergency-stop and LOGS the outcome rather than asserting it, with the comment 'the Plan/Prepare outcome itself is LOGGED rather than asserted, on purpose: asserting the defect would pin it in place and turn its future repair into a test failure in a file that task cannot edit' (framing_test.go:562-564) and 'V2-085 owns the repair' (framing_test.go:610). This task is that repair, and converting that log into an assertion is part of it.

decisions.decision: The permit kind is domain.PermitClaim for BOTH commands. Not PermitIntake, and no new PermitKind. The resulting seven-mode behaviour is identical for both and is the design: allow ALLOWS, pause-intake ALLOWS, pause-claim DENIES, graceful-stop DENIES, immediate-stop DENIES, emergency-stop DENIES, cancel DENIES -- two of seven.
decisions.rationale: Derived from the measured gate at internal/domain/control.go:266-281 (permitAllowed) against the product's own definitions of the two pause modes, not chosen for symmetry. (i) PermitIntake is REJECTED. permitAllowed returns kind != PermitIntake under pause-intake, so intake-gated commands are denied there; docs/product/definition.md:142 defines pause intake as stopping the reception of NEW Requirements or their entry into the queue. Planning an Increment for a Requirement that is already captured, and readying an Increment that is already proposed, are finishing what you already have, so denying them under pause-intake would silently turn pause-intake into a full stop -- the exact error V2-082 d5 refused for start-framing. (ii) PermitClaim is ACCEPTED. definition.md:143 defines pause claim as stopping the claim of NEW work, and the two commands are precisely what makes work claimable: Plan creates the Increment and Prepare puts it in the only status Claim accepts. internal/application/allocation.go:373 records the same reading from the scheduler's side -- 'ready maps to scheduler.StatusReady: this is the only schedulable status'. Withholding the readying of new work while claims are paused is what pause-claim exists to do. (iii) A new PermitKind is REJECTED: it would require editing internal/domain, which is prohibited, and it would oblige every existing mode to be re-argued. (iv) Consistency is a secondary, not the primary, argument: Service.StartFraming already uses PermitClaim for the sibling edge in the same lifecycle (internal/application/framing.go:183), so the three commands that carry a Requirement or its Increment forward now share one gate and one table.

decisions.decision: The decision is evaluated with domain.Permit ONLY. Nothing from either command is passed to domain.EffectFromPermit, and neither command stages an OutboxItem. Service.effectOutbox (service.go:1636-1700) is not called.
decisions.rationale: Two measured reasons, and the first is decisive. (a) domain.EffectFromPermit (internal/domain/control.go:296-320) refuses unless current.Mode is EXACTLY ControlAllow -- the L3 closure V2-059 measured and docs/product/definition.md:150-154 states as product behaviour. Routing Plan and Prepare through it would deny them under pause-intake as well, which contradicts d2's whole argument, and would deny them under pause-claim for the wrong reason. The gate must be the per-kind table, not the allow-only closure. (b) Neither command asks anything outside the control plane to do anything: no forge call, no deploy, no credential. domain.PermitKind.SideEffect() is false for PermitClaim (control.go:199-201), so there is nothing for an effect to carry. Staging an outbox item would additionally change the outbox row count that internal/application/stop_matrix_test.go's dispatcher pass counts, for no gain.

decisions.decision: The ControlTarget and the revision are resolved INSIDE each transaction from the aggregate graph, never from the request. Neither PlanRequest nor PrepareRequest gains a control_revision, a repository_id or a timestamp field, so no transport contract changes and contracts_changed is empty. Plan resolves the link it already reads, u.RequirementRepositoryLink(ctx, req.RequirementID), and MOVES that read to before anything is staged. Prepare resolves it from the Increment's own parent, u.RequirementRepositoryLink(ctx, inc.RequirementID.String()). Both then build domain.ControlTarget{InstallationID: s.config.InstallationID, RepositoryID: linked} and take the revision from domain.EffectiveControl(controls, target), using 0 when the effective control is not Found.
decisions.rationale: Three measured constraints force this and one makes it cheap. ServiceConfig deliberately holds no repository id (service.go:153-160, V2-071 A6): an Installation registers many Repositories, so a per-process id would make a domain.ScopeRepository intent match the wrong one. Capture derives its revision exactly this way (service.go:816-824) and Plan already resolves the link this way, only later in the callback (service.go:947-960), so this is a re-ordering rather than a new read. And a caller-supplied revision would be a trap: domain.Permit refuses unless request.ControlRevision equals control.Revision exactly, so a caller that had not re-read controls would be denied for a reason unrelated to the owner's intent. Deriving it internally makes the exactness check trivially true and leaves the mode as the only thing that can deny -- which is what the seven-mode table must measure. Because no request field is added, contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml is untouched and this task does NOT enrol in the api-contract chain: measured, Plan and Prepare have no HTTP route at all, and openapi-v1.yaml:6-8 says so in as many words ('Increment decomposition/planning is intentionally not a public owner operation; it remains a loop scheduler responsibility').

decisions.decision: The order inside each s.mutate callback is fixed and is part of the design: (1) u.Idempotency replay, including the fingerprint-conflict refusal, FIRST; (2) load the aggregate and check the expected version; (3) resolve the link, read u.Controls, compute domain.EffectiveControl and evaluate domain.Permit; (4) only then stage anything. A denied call stages no aggregate, no event and no idempotency record, and returns domain.ErrControlDenied unwrapped enough for errors.Is to see it.
decisions.rationale: The replay must stay ahead of the Permit for the same reason Capture's does (service.go:781-788): a retry of a request that already committed must reproduce the committed response, and a stop engaged after the commit must not turn a completed operation into a refusal -- that would make the idempotency guarantee depend on the control mode. Placing the Permit after the version check keeps the refusal attributable: a stale version is still domain.ErrStaleVersion and an unknown id is still ErrNotFound, so the seven-mode table measures the mode and nothing else. Staging nothing on a denial is what makes non_goals item 2 ('do not turn a refusal into a silent no-op') checkable: the refusal is an error AND the store is byte-unchanged, and both halves are asserted.

decisions.decision: The seven-mode behaviour is asserted per command in a NEW test file, internal/application/planning_permit_test.go, following the idiom framing_test.go and human_input_test.go already use: an explicit want table, cross-checked in the same run against the package's existing permitAllowedTable mirror (internal/application/stop_matrix_test.go:242) and against Capture's MEASURED intake behaviour at the same control revision. stopMatrixKinds and wantStopMatrixCells in stop_matrix_test.go are NOT widened, wantStopModeAllowedCounts is NOT changed, and docs/product/definition.md is NOT edited.
decisions.rationale: Measured reason for not widening the matrix: docs/product/definition.md:155-162 states the figures 7 modes x 8 kinds = 56 cells and 12 allowed cells and then scopes them by name -- 'このcell数はinternal/applicationのTestStopModeByKindMatrixが検証している'. The document's claim is about that named test's eight kinds, so as long as stopMatrixKinds stays at eight the document stays true and the docs component key does not move. Adding two kinds would make it 70 cells and 14 allowed, forcing a docs edit, a docs-chain serialization and a re-derivation of a figure V2-059 already had to correct once. V2-082 set the precedent one task earlier by putting start-framing's table in framing_test.go rather than in the matrix (framing_test.go:227-249). The cross-check against Capture in the same run is what makes the table an argument rather than a copy: under pause-intake the two must DISAGREE, Plan and Prepare allowed and a fresh Capture denied, and that disagreement is the whole case for d2.

decisions.decision: Existing tests are expected to pass unchanged, and where one does not, the implementer must classify the failure before touching anything: either (A) the intended guard fired because the fixture engages a non-allow mode and then plans or prepares, or (B) the fixture simply never set a control mode. Class B cannot fail and must be reported as a design error if it does. Class A is fixed in the FIXTURE -- by establishing the Increment before the Control Intent, as stop_matrix_test.go already does -- and never by relaxing the guard, widening the accepted modes, or passing a caller-supplied revision.
decisions.rationale: Measured, and the measurement says the blast radius should be near zero. 22 test files call Plan or Prepare (`grep -rn '\.Plan(\|\.PlanIncrement(\|\.Prepare(\|\.PrepareIncrement(' --include='*_test.go' .`, 14 of the hits in internal/application/service_test.go alone). A fixture that sets no Control Intent gets domain.EffectiveControl{Mode: ControlAllow, Found: false} and revision 0, which domain.Permit allows (control.go:238-247 defaults an empty mode to ControlAllow and accepts revision 0 when nothing is Found), so every such fixture is unaffected. The two fixtures that DO engage a mode both build their increments first: internal/application/stop_matrix_test.go:120-138 calls prepareIncrement twice and only then calls Control, and internal/application/human_input_test.go:960-968 builds its fixture before the Control Intent for exactly the stated reason. So the expected disagreement count is zero, which is precisely why any failure must be classified rather than absorbed.

decisions.decision: internal/application/framing_test.go:565 TestPlanAndPrepareAreMeasuredUnderEmergencyStop keeps its name and becomes an ASSERTION: under emergency-stop, Plan and Prepare must now be refused with domain.ErrControlDenied and must leave the Requirement, the Increment and the event count byte-unchanged, while Service.StartFraming stays refused as before. Its doc comment keeps the V2-082 history -- that the outcome used to be logged, and why -- rather than deleting it.
decisions.rationale: The test was written to be flipped: framing_test.go:610 names V2-085 as the owner of the repair, and the reason given for logging rather than asserting was that the repairing task would need to edit a file V2-082 could not. That reason expires here. Keeping the name satisfies the constraint that every pre-existing top-level test keeps its name and keeps passing; keeping the history in the comment is what stops the next reader from having to guess whether an assertion is a claim or a fossil.

decisions.decision: No route, no read model, no domain edit, no new command, and no change to what either command does when permission is granted. internal/domain, internal/api, contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml, internal/application/readmodels.go and internal/web are prohibited BY DESIGN. PlanResponse and PrepareResponse keep their exact shapes and their exact success values.
decisions.rationale: Measured: neither command has an HTTP route -- there is no h.plan or h.prepare in internal/api, and openapi-v1.yaml:6-8 declares increment decomposition deliberately absent from the public surface -- so the defect lives entirely at the application boundary and is fixed entirely there. Adding a route would be a second, larger design that this outcome does not ask for and that V2-086 must settle first (who may call it). No read model changes because no status, field or response shape changes: a denied Plan leaves exactly the state a Plan that was never called leaves. non_goals item 3 ('do not change what the two commands do when permission is granted') is checkable precisely because the success path is untouched: every existing assertion about PlanResponse.Version and PrepareResponse.Version must still hold byte-for-byte.

decisions.decision: internal/runner/orchestrator.go is NOT edited by this task, and its journey must keep passing byte-for-byte. Its Plan and Prepare calls become permit-gated; because its fixture engages no Control Intent they stay allowed. That the journey reaches them through a caller the component fabricates for itself (orchestrator.go:39, application.Caller{Role: RoleOwner, Subject: 'runner-local-owner'}) is a separate defect owned by V2-086 and is recorded here, not fixed.
decisions.rationale: Measured: Orchestrator.RunFakeJourney has exactly ONE caller in the whole repository and it is internal/runner/orchestrator_test.go:56; cmd/runner/main.go wires no control plane at all and exits 2 without --fake. So the journey is a test driver, its Plan and Prepare calls run under no control mode, and this task's guard cannot reach them. Recording that rather than relabelling the caller keeps the two repairs separable and keeps internal/runner out of this task's paths.

decisions.decision: Quota is measured, not assumed. Each command gains one keyed read of the Requirement-to-Repository link (Prepare) or re-orders one it already performs (Plan), plus one read of the Control Intent collection. Both must stay inside quota.MutationUsage, measured at Reads 32 / Writes 16 (internal/quota/quota.go:62). If either does not fit, stop and escalate; internal/quota is prohibited and no budget is raised.
decisions.rationale: s.mutate reserves quota.MutationUsage once per transaction before the callback can stage anything (service.go:142-152), so a command that outgrows the reservation fails closed rather than overspending -- which is correct behaviour but would surface as an unrelated failure. Capture already performs exactly this pair of reads inside one mutate reservation (service.go:809-824), so the shape is known to fit; the point of measuring is to record it rather than to infer it. The separate hazard -- that the in-memory adapter never calls quota.Counter.TrueUp, so quota.ReadTransactionUsage (Reads 6001, Writes 1) admits only four READ transactions per budget day -- does not bind here because both commands are mutations, but any new test that also reads through Service must advance the injected clock rather than weaken its assertions. That adapter defect is V2-087's.

risks: d2 is the single point the whole task rests on, and it departs from the intake precedent Capture sets. If the implementer reads the control gate differently -- for instance concluding that Plan should be denied under pause-intake because a new Increment is new work -- that is a design disagreement, not an implementation detail: stop and escalate. Do not resolve it by removing the Permit, by choosing PermitIntake, or by adding a PermitKind, which would require editing internal/domain.

22 test files call Plan or Prepare. The measurement says none of them should break, because a fixture with no Control Intent is allowed and the two fixtures that engage a mode build their increments first. A break therefore means either the guard is wrong or a fixture is doing something the census did not see; both are escalations, and neither is fixed by relaxing the guard.

internal/application/service.go is held by V2-083, which is queued and lists it in allowed_paths together with internal/api/api.go and six other files in internal/application. Running V2-083 and V2-085 concurrently produces a conflict in service.go. Serialize V2-085 after V2-083.

internal/application/framing_test.go is V2-082's file and this task rewrites the body of one test in it. If V2-084 is also allowed that file, the two tasks conflict; V2-084 must be serialized after V2-085.

Widening stopMatrixKinds would look like the natural place for the new table and would silently invalidate docs/product/definition.md:155-162, which cites 56 cells and 12 allowed cells and names TestStopModeByKindMatrix as the verifier. The eight-kind matrix and the document must both be left alone.

The refusal must be an error and not a no-op. A Permit failure returned as nil with an unchanged store would pass a naive 'canonical state did not move' assertion while violating non_goals item 2, so both halves -- errors.Is(err, domain.ErrControlDenied) AND a byte-unchanged store -- are asserted for every denied cell.
